description: A C# game engine in which a program opens a window, draws each frame with plain static calls named as raylib's functions are, and draws Dear ImGui in the same frame, over SDL3, Vulkan and Slang, with an ECS and source-generated behaviors underneath.
releaseNotes:
Every descriptor pool is counted from the layouts whose sets it gives, so a pass given another binding still draws on macOS, and a frame that fails waits for the device so no pool an earlier frame reads is destroyed.
Reads the probes at the surface itself rather than half a spacing off it, so a hit beside a wall takes the light that reaches the wall.
Ends the last cascade's interval at the field's edge, so its rays across a room wider than four times its spacing meet the far wall rather than ending in mid-air.
Records the reads at no lean measured again on four rays a texel, which widen the grazing floor at Low through the light past its last cascade.
Sends four rays a texel in any cascade of eight texels a side, so Low and Medium read the grazing floor's room as High does.
Records the gain's cause as the light's gradient between the probes and the walls, and three mends of it measured and not kept.
Splits each face in gi.probe's report by where its ways were met and records the light past the first bounce at the world probes' own hits by bounce.
Records the ways turned for each tile and the thirty-six ways as measured and not kept, since each widens four views' distance to their references at both sizes.
Records the openness ratio on the light past the first bounce as measured and not kept, since it moves the open middle and lowers the wall's foot.
The rendering notes record that a corner's surfaces take the light past the first bounce from probes standing in more open light than the corner, which carries what remains of its excess.
A ray's hit in the scene's field takes its color from the cells whose surface faces its way, so a wall's light beside a corner keeps the wall's own color rather than the one beside it.
The screen's march takes a ray as meeting a surface only where the depth does not leap across the step it crossed it in, so a ray passing behind a thin wall's end reads what lies beyond it, and the march has a shader module of its own.
The rendering notes record how far a screen probe's sixteen fixed ways stand from the light around it and what four ways of turning them gained and cost, none of them kept.
Screen probes past the first cascade of light probes send their rays as far as those within it, so a room's far corner no longer takes the light a coarser probe sees of the lamp-lit surfaces near it.
The first cascade of light probes sends four rays along each of its directions and takes their light together, so a bright spot under a lamp no longer stands for a whole direction's light.
The gi.probe console command lists the ways that carry most of the face furthest from the reference, each with where its ray went, its merged light, its own ray's and the reference's.
Screen probes read the light beyond their rays where each ray ends and keep the rays that pass behind a surface or off the screen, so walls lit across open space take the reference's light, and a bounce test allows 3% where 2% for a tint now 1.212 against 1.240.
A console command reads each of the sixteen rays of the screen probe under a pixel, where it was met and its light, against a path-traced reference along its way and over the ways it stands for.
A pixel no screen probe on a surface like its own stands near reads the world's probes it sees through the field, so the thin room's corner takes no light from the lamp outside its walls.
A mesh of many small emitters, as Ore's ore, is cut into its parts and carried as glow lights, each from the faces of its box it shows, so the ground beside the ore takes its light smoothly and within 2% of a path-traced reference.
The ImGui pass draws each command with the texture it names, so a program's texture given an id by GetImGuiTextureId is drawn in an ImGui window, and the font atlas where a command names none.
A setting chooses where the sun's contact shadows through the scene's distance field darken its light, everywhere, past the shadow map's reach alone or nowhere, so a shadow the map holds may keep its hard edge.
A particle emitter may keep its particles in its entity's space, turning with it and its parent, and hold particles the program places at points there, which an example of a turning sky shows.
The gamepad example draws raylib's picture of a PlayStation pad for a pad SDL3 names so and its picture of an Xbox pad for every other, both kept with the examples under CC0, and its capture is taken again.
The light global illumination gives is read against path-traced references in the examples that draw it and in Ore, with six faults pictured, measured and placed in the cascades.
The schedule test's log provider keeps an exception's type name and not the object, and the script generation test names what may hold a generation that outlives its collections.
The leak test says the private bytes beside a held driver without judging them, and a memory failure's message puts the series after every ten apps and the heaps before the allocation lines.
The leak test allows the driver's thread handles that its census finds kept and judges its heap floor on the live objects, and the physics plugin warms its solver once.
The measure's record gives models_directional_billboard three points of room, since its share follows the runner's processor, within a point of 5.5 on an AMD EPYC 9V45 and 7.8 to 7.9 on an AMD EPYC 7763.
The leak test names the threads behind the handles each followed app's steps open and keep, on Windows each Thread handle's thread with its name and whether it has ended and on Linux each thread started and ended, and a handle failure's message puts its series and what each app kept before its steps.
Ore joins the games, a voxel landscape of 48 by 48 columns under global illumination whose emissive ore is its only light at night, walked in the first person, and played, soaked, resized and captured with the others.
The two drawing leak tests make their apps with the validation layer off on every system, since the layer's Windows build at 1.4.363.0 kept about a megabyte each time the loader unloaded it, and a failure's message names where a climb lies before its series.
The voxel game leaves the engine's tree for its own repository, Voxel-Sandbox, its two projects removed with their lines in the solution and in AGENTS.md, and the guides and RENDERING.md cite it there with the numbers as measured.
The measure against raylib says its processor in a notice on every run, so a run that holds names the processor its pairs held on, and the pairs measured for the first time share the other nine notices GitHub shows.
The leak test's held instance enables the validation layer wherever the loader offers it, so the layer stays loaded through the hundred apps, and the Windows job takes LunarG's SDK at 1.4.363.0, the version Linux pins and the latest, in place of whatever is latest.
On Windows the leak test sweeps the address space at every step of its four followed apps and names the private data allocations each step added, with their sizes and how many still stand at the app's end and after the next app, its memory instruments moved to a file of their own.
The measure against raylib says the processor it ran on and whether gfni is among its flags, on its errors and in a summary of its pairs, and keeps both pictures of every pair with the captures, so a pair's frames are compared between runs.
The leak test sweeps the address space on Windows at the twentieth app and the last for its committed memory by the kind of region holding it, and before each app's last reading waits half a second at most for its threads, which every app's threads met on Linux but two in eighty, with what changes between apps a step of its own.
The measure against raylib says the pairs that fail as errors with their shares and their room, and a failed step names only the games that ended other than of their own or still run, after its last lines.
The leak test reads what each step of every app's life takes of the process's memory, averaged over the apps after the twentieth, and on Windows what the process's heaps hold allocated and committed, so a failure names the step whose memory is not given back.
The leak test's held instance asks for portability drivers where the loader offers them, as the engine's instance does, so MoltenVK gives it an instance on macOS.
The held instance's comment says what the loader does on every system and keeps to the line width.
Every cache of Mesa's shaders is keyed by the processor, examples open through build/open-game.sh, whose line says whether gfni is among the flags and what Mesa's cache served, and the leak test reads the collector's committed bytes and runs its hundred apps once more beside a Vulkan instance it holds.
Every game a Linux or macOS job plays is opened by build/open-game.sh, which waits on it and writes how it ended, and on Linux prints the processor at each opening and reads with gdb the core a game that dies leaves, which drive-game.sh, step.py, soak-check.py and storm.sh say.
Every way an app ends logs a line with its exit code last, drive-game.sh starts a game under a shell that writes how it ended and reads the kernel and memory where one dies on Linux, the leak test reads the private bytes on Windows, Manor and Swarm are bounded by what a whole walk or turn holds, and prose says what a thing is in place of a likeness or an idiom.
Prose uses the technical terms global illumination, emissive and controlling or scripting through the command line and keeps colons out of running sentences, as the Register section and the colon rule of STYLE.md ask, and the command line's guide is docs/command-line.md.
A pipeline's entry point name and the instance's program name are written null-terminated on the stack, where a collection that moved the array a pointer read them from left a pipeline named nothing and a lamp's shadow undrawn, and a test makes pipelines while the heap is compacted.
Two workflows do the work of four, build.yml on a push with what the pack run adds behind its pack input and pack.yml running it before the pack.
The review's record of the runs of fc5fdc97 is committed alone.
The script test's grow mode is given a minute and grows in random bytes, so its memory limit comes before its time limit on a slow runner.
The drawing leak test reads its resident baseline after the heap census it takes, and a reference frame waits until every model its scene places has loaded before it settles.
A session file that cannot be opened for a moment is read again, the puzzle's drive counts each frame a sixtieth of a second so a slow device sees its swipe, and a game that dies off Windows leaves a dump.
The strategy game's long wait in the examples job takes ten minutes to answer, and the commit with no sentence that carried a pass of this file is listed among those rule N 7.2 allows.
An entity an AnimatedModel draws gives its body the model's meshes as the clip last posed them, so a mesh or a hull collider on it makes a body where it was refused.
Light that scatters under a surface stays out of render textures and probe faces, since a render texture holds no linear frame and a probe's faces span a few pixels of a reach.
A test holds the subsurface thickness a material gives as a cap on the thickness measured, a sheet the field holds a cell thick lit through by the two millimeters given.
The commit that ignores the Voxel-Sandbox folder, whose message has no sentence, is listed among those rule N 7.2 allows.
A failed suite saves the shaders Mesa compiled, the Windows suite is held to 60 minutes, the leak test's message carries its resident series, and the macOS captures run in the pack run alone.
The voxel game has furnaces that smelt meat, sand, cobblestone, iron ore and logs over coal, charcoal and wood, iron ore in the stone with iron tools, and hearts and food outlined so they read over any color.
The voxel game leaves undrawn the sections the eye cannot see through open cells, flooding from the eye's section across the faces each section's open cells join as Minecraft's visibility graph does.
A glow light's march ends its way out of a surface where it left it, so the light past a pillar's edge rises on the wall behind without a step.
Opaque materials draw with pipelines that fold the alpha test's discard away, for the devices that turn their early depth test off under one.
The voxel game spawns zombies, skeletons, spiders and creepers in the dark in survival, which hunt the player along the blocks, strike, shoot arrows or explode, burn by day and drop their loot.
The voxel game writes a relit section's colors in place beside its packed bytes, so the light that bounces and its reference take a change of light in the frame after.
Vertex colors written in place reach the light that bounces and the reference in the frame after, the field painting again the cells a recolored mesh is nearest against its cascade's kept words and the ray scene rewriting its corners.
The voxel game opens the engine's window of the effects over the frame from its own, and its light settings read the bloom and exposure back from the engine.
Each effect over the frame is read back beside its setter, and DrawPostProcessWindow shows and sets every one in an ImGui window of its own while the picture is looked at.
The screen's probes' rays reach twice as far as the world's probes are apart where they end in the finest cascade, and a ray that went behind the depth and off the picture is handed to the field from where it stood in front, so a wall before a pillar sees it and a closed room keeps the light outside it out.
The voxel game gives the player health, food and breath in survival, hurts falls, drowning, starving and cactus, feeds the player bread, apples and raw meat, and spills the inventory at a death before a new life at the spawn.
A mesh that moved settles into the scene's field only after standing 1,024 frames, and a frame where meshes moved in their places is read by place, so walking figures that pause rebuild no cascade and cost the field a few microseconds a box.
The voxel game crafts in a grid of the inventory and at a crafting table, with wooden and stone tools that break their blocks faster and wear out, coal in the stone, and stone that drops nothing without a pickaxe.
The voxel game draws its mobs with BouncesLight off, so they keep their shadows and cost the scene field nothing as they walk.
A material's BouncesLight, true unless set, leaves a mesh that moves in most frames out of the scene's field, the glow lights and the bounce's reference while it casts its shadows.
The screen's probes find the frame before's light where each probe stood rather than by its tile's middle, a pixel off, so a still view's blend no longer drifts toward the probes to its right and below.
The voxel game plays in creative or survival mode, with an inventory, blocks that take time to break and drop what they leave, mobs that drop their loot, and stacks on the ground that the player picks up and throws.
The voxel game has pigs, cows, sheep, chickens and villagers that find their way through the blocks, run when hit, go home at night through their doors and are saved with their columns.
A probe's path-traced reference leaves out the glow of an emitter the bounce carries as a light where a path first meets it, as the probe's rays do.
Gives the GPU no colors or second texture coordinates for a mesh of positions alone, its colors kept for the light field to read.
Gives the light that bounces a guide page of its own, the radiance cascades, the field, the probes, the qualities' costs, the limits and the tools, and names it in the README.
Names the flat API's class E3D, its files, the tests' and every program's using line following, the namespace and the package as they were.
The voxel game draws its sections and clouds from positions and eight packed bytes a vertex in a stream of its own, and a relight writes the packed bytes alone.
Names the development machine's GPU in place of its model wherever a user reads, in the tests, the shaders and the guides, keeping every measurement.
Lets a mesh be uploaded from its positions alone, twelve bytes a vertex, its stream packing the rest, with every pipeline that binds a vertex reading it so.
Lets a mesh carry a vertex stream of the program's own, read as CUSTOM0 and written in place, and makes the pack wait on the examples job.
Runs the examples job from a workflow of its own, a push building every game and playing one, the pack run capturing, measuring, playing and soaking them all.
Counts the examples under the README's Examples heading and the pictures in each row of its gallery, written and checked by the examples table's script.
Gives the suite run by build/test.py an NVIDIA driver cache of its own above the driver's cap, where a full one compiled every pipeline again and failed some.
Draws a frame where no light bounces through a build of the model pass that leaves the bounce out with the glow lights, a fifth of the whole fragment stage.
Fits a capture to the gallery's size with cwebp where it is installed, so the examples job needs no ImageMagick, and names a first game step that fails.
Removes games/Pusher, Slide taking its place as the game CI builds, publishes native and plays in a window, and opens the README's guide with the cheat sheet.
